name: Simprosys Google Shopping Feed
winningEvidence: Established distribution: Shopify App Store snapshot on 29 September 2026 shows a 4.9 rating from 4,894 reviews and a 16 August 2017 launch. Selection as a commercial benchmark is warranted; ratings do not prove incremental AI-shopping purchases (app).

Vendor claims 90K+ Shopify merchants; independent active/paid-customer verification was not found. Qualitative merchants value syncing and support, but controlled Simprosys conversion studies were not found in the reviewed official sources (product, reviews).

Low verified pricing and variant-inclusive billing create a demanding baseline for an entrant. This does not establish Simprosys profitability or imply that low price means weaker execution (pricing).
currentOffer: Shopify merchants use it to distribute and manage product feeds and related advertising/tracking operations. Observed 29 September 2026, USD/month: 500 published products 4.99; 1,000 8.99; 5,000 13.99; 10,000 17.99. Variants are not counted separately; billing is based on published products, not submitted products. First installation has a 21-day trial. AI enrichment is USD 1 per 25 products one-time; XML and additional market feeds have separate fees. Google, Microsoft, Meta and Pinterest integrations, rules, metafields and Markets support are documented (pricing, product).
conversionMechanism: The feed can establish product eligibility and convey relevant facts, accurate offers and delivery information; merchant landing and checkout execution must then complete the purchase. Shopify documents Merchant Center, including third-party feeds, as the Google AI Mode/Gemini discovery route. Its ChatGPT channel instead uses Shopify Catalog and the merchant's online checkout. A Simprosys-only feed edit therefore cannot be presumed to alter ChatGPT data. Track the exact destination and checkout path before measuring impact (google-ai, chatgpt-shopify).

harness.details: Here liveMonitoring means observations of named consumer AI shopping outputs: none was found in reviewed Simprosys official pages. Feed/campaign status and live advertising reports are documented (zombie). No Simprosys offline shopping simulation or in-app randomized AI-shopping experiment was found; its blog recommends A/B testing (simprosys-ab), which is not a native implementation claim. GA4/GTM purchase tracking is documented (ga4), but source attribution is not causal incrementality and storefront pixels do not cover every embedded checkout (google-ai). These are source-search findings, not proof private or new features do not exist. DataFeedWatch already documents title A/B allocation by item ID (dfw-ab).

strengths: Low published price with variants included, mature Shopify distribution and qualitative support evidence make replacement on basic feed operations unattractive.
Rules, source mapping, Markets feeds, generated enrichment with review, campaign operations, delivery integration and checkout setup already cover much of a generic AI-commerce feature list.
Simprosys can contribute to Google AI discovery through an actual Merchant Center integration path; this is more concrete than an undifferentiated AI readiness score.
Existing tracking and operational integrations can support a complementary experiment product without rebuilding feed transport.
limits: AI enrichment guide specifies English stores, selected categories and descriptions longer than 200 characters, and says changed products do not automatically re-optimise (ai).

Merchant Center approval and successful submission do not verify every downstream offer, chosen variant or checkout requirement. Native platforms also perform checks, so residual error prevalence needs measurement.

Published merchant testimonials do not supply randomized purchase effects, denominators, refunds or attribution completeness. No supportable Simprosys-specific incremental AI conversion percentage was found.
Google and ChatGPT use different data routes; updating an ad feed need not change a Shopify Catalog record. Native mapping already exists (mapping).
Per-channel checkout constraints limit what a merchant app can repair or measure. No tool reviewed reveals proprietary production ranking, personalization or candidate retrieval.
improve: Begin with reproduced, order-relevant failures for current Simprosys users and use the app as the transport layer. Compare against existing support and native configuration before charging.
Separate feed acceptance, consumer-facing propagation, correct variant landing, valid cart and kept purchase into distinct observations.
Prioritize variant handoff and source-change expiry as bounded pilots; compatibility and pack identity merit narrow vertical pilots only where authoritative evidence exists.

Use a frozen search proxy to test sensitivity and screen candidate repairs. Preserve real-engine monitoring as observational evidence and reserve causal claims for merchant-controlled randomized purchase experiments.
Sell measured extra retained contribution or a concrete repair, with the low incumbent price as the buyer's alternative. Proposed pilot prices below are unvalidated, not market demand.

ideas.title: Expire enriched facts when their source product changes
ideas.buyer: A Shopify merchant with frequently revised apparel, furniture or hardware products already using Simprosys.
ideas.problem: An optimized attribute can remain plausible after its supporting specification changes; an accepted feed can therefore answer the shopper's constraint incorrectly.
ideas.mechanism: Discovery and selection: a dependency-triggered correction can restore eligibility for the right query and prevent a misleading recommendation. Purchases increase only if changed facts are reaching a shopping surface and were suppressing suitable demand.
ideas.intervention: Record source-field and supplier-revision dependencies for generated facts. On a material edit, invalidate only affected facts, obtain merchant-approved replacement facts and publish them through the correct route: Merchant Center for Google or Shopify sources for Catalog. Verify destination and landing evidence before calling the repair complete.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Simprosys already has AI enrichment and manual approval; its guide explicitly says updates do not automatically trigger re-optimisation. Feed refresh itself is not missing. Shopify mapping already chooses preferred sources.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A small add-on can detect a narrow class of semantically stale enrichment that ordinary successful-sync checks miss. The hypothesized advantage is measurable retained orders after verified propagation, not more generated attributes.
dataNeeded: Versioned product edits and approved supplier specifications
Generated-field dependencies and destination snapshots
Product-family order, refund and AI-source attribution data
ideas.experiment: Randomize product families with upcoming routine revisions to dependency-triggered refresh or the merchant's normal reviewed refresh workflow; repair urgent false claims immediately in both arms. Use a predeclared propagation period, then 6-8 weeks or the powered sample. Primary endpoint: kept AI-origin orders per assigned family-week. Track total orders, disputes and return reasons; do not pool variants independently.
ideas.metric: Difference in kept orders with observable AI provenance per randomized family-week, adjusted only for pre-period order levels; total kept orders are a guardrail. Missing referral provenance remains unknown.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized purchase effect. The source establishes a refresh limitation, not its prevalence or loss rate (ai); separate destination routes are documented (google-ai, chatgpt-shopify).

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative monthly fee USD 29; measured incremental contribution per kept order denoted m; no traffic or conversion baseline assumed.
impactScenario.calculation: Required extra kept orders = 29/m, before service costs. At an illustrative m = USD 20, break-even is 1.45 orders, or 2 whole extra orders.
impactScenario.range: Effect can be zero if facts rarely change or engines use another source, and negative if correction breaks a valid mapping.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated value-based pilot: USD 29/month above the existing feed app, contingent on a demonstrated stale-fact incident and retained-order value.
ideas.costControl: Hash source dependencies and regenerate only changed claims; avoid repeated whole-catalogue LLM jobs.
dependencies: Merchant permission to read source revisions and publish to the appropriate destination
A reliable canonical product identity
Enough revised products and orders for clustered inference
ideas.failureMode: A source edit might be cosmetic, or the supposed canonical source might be wrong; over-invalidation can remove useful information.
ideas.falsifier: Observed revisions do not create consequential stale facts, or a powered rollout finds no incremental kept orders and no operational benefit worth its price.

ideas.title: Keep the chosen variant intact from recommendation to cart
ideas.buyer: Multi-variant merchants receiving AI referral traffic through Shopify storefronts.
ideas.problem: The referral names a particular size, finish or pack, but redirects, theme scripts or locale changes can reset the selected variant.
ideas.mechanism: Landing and checkout: preserving the shopper's already-made choice removes reselection and wrong-item carting, which may convert arrivals that would otherwise leave. It cannot create AI discovery by itself.
ideas.intervention: Build owned-store browser probes that compare offered variant identity, rendered controls, displayed price and actual cart line. Repair approved URL/redirect/theme rules and carry country and quantity where supported. Run probes after theme releases; never assume a 200 response proves a working cart.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Simprosys provides variant feeds and a direct-checkout tutorial; Google already checks checkout URLs and requires variant alignment. The proposed edge is verification through the merchant's real theme/cart behavior across locales.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: Merchant-specific redirect and JavaScript failures survive generic feed validation often enough to justify continuous probes.
dataNeeded: Canonical variant IDs and listing URLs
Redirect, selected-control and cart-line traces across locales/devices
Assigned visitor IDs, completed orders and wrong-variant returns
ideas.experiment: After fixing any severe known error universally, persistently randomize eligible AI-referred visitors between current supported routing and the verified variant-preserving route. Run 4-8 weeks plus return maturation, with sample size based on actual purchase frequency. Primary endpoint: kept orders per assigned visitor. Guard against slower loads, inaccessible selectors and accidental cart overwrites.
ideas.metric: Intent-to-treat kept-order probability among all eligible randomized arrivals, including visitors who never add to cart; variant correction rate is a diagnostic only.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized uplift; known variant/landing requirements and recurring Google URL validation are adjacent infrastructure evidence (variant, checkout), not Simprosys-specific failure rates.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative 2,000 eligible arrivals/month and USD 49/month fee; baseline purchase probability must be measured.
impactScenario.calculation: Extra kept orders = 2,000 × observed absolute purchase-probability difference. At USD 25 contribution/order, fee break-even is 1.96 extra orders, about 0.098 percentage points.
impactScenario.range: Zero if routing already preserves choices; negative if a repair changes the wrong variant or creates latency.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated pilot USD 49/month for stores with reproduced failures; the fee must compete with simply fixing the theme once.
ideas.costControl: Probe representative high-traffic route/variant combinations plus changed templates; use deterministic checks before model interpretation.
dependencies: Theme or redirect fix access
A permitted cart test mechanism without placing orders
Reliable visitor assignment and order linkage
ideas.failureMode: Most stores already preserve variants, or AI referrals arrive without enough variant context to recover a choice.
ideas.falsifier: A representative audit finds negligible variant loss, or correct routing fails to raise kept-order probability at useful precision.

ideas.title: Offer deadline-feasible fulfilment when the shopper needs it by a date
ideas.buyer: Gift, replacement-part and event-supply merchants with dependable fulfilment data.
ideas.problem: A broad shipping estimate does not answer whether this variant can reach this postcode before the shopper's stated deadline.
ideas.mechanism: Selection and checkout: a currently feasible delivery or pickup option can retain deadline-sensitive buyers. The benefit comes from resolving a real timing constraint, not displaying artificial urgency.
ideas.intervention: Combine exact stock location, processing cutoff, holidays and carrier service estimates into a timestamped quote for a shopper-provided deadline. Recheck before checkout and surface merchant-supported pickup or another service on the storefront when appropriate. Keep feed cutoff fields synchronized.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Simprosys already supplies Google-calculated delivery estimates; Google has product/country handling cutoffs. Google AI direct checkout does not currently support local pickup/delivery, so those alternatives require a supported merchant-store route.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: Operational exceptions and precise deadlines create a useful gap beyond aggregate historical estimates, particularly after cutoffs or during stock-location changes.
dataNeeded: Shopper-provided postcode/deadline
Stock locations, warehouse calendars and live carrier options
Promised and actual delivery dates, kept orders and cancellations
ideas.experiment: Randomize eligible AI-referred visitors who enter a deadline, keeping the same input burden in both arms. Compare the current accurate shipping explanation with a feasible-option quote. Plan 6-8 weeks including cutoff transitions; power from actual deadline traffic. Primary endpoint: kept purchases delivered within the stated deadline per assigned visitor. Guardrails: total kept purchases, missed promises and support contacts.
ideas.metric: On-time kept-order probability per prequalified randomized visitor; report completed-order probability separately so faster delivery is not mistaken for extra purchases.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized effect; existing estimate and cutoff capabilities are documented (delivery, cutoff). No cited source measures this proposed deadline intervention.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative USD 49 monthly pilot; the store must measure deadline-eligible traffic and contribution.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even extra on-time kept orders = (49 + incremental fulfilment costs)/incremental contribution per order; do not count orders merely moved between shipping services as incremental.
impactScenario.range: May be zero when buyers already trust existing estimates; negative if forecasts are wrong or faster fulfilment costs exceed retained demand.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 49/month plus merchant delivery costs, tested only with merchants reporting actual deadline abandonment.
ideas.costControl: Cache stable calendars and carrier zones; fetch live quotes only for expressed deadline intent.
dependencies: Warehouse and carrier integration
Honest delivery confidence and fallback behavior
Storefront checkout for unsupported delivery methods
ideas.failureMode: Carrier reliability or stock accuracy is insufficient, producing more missed promises than useful assurance.
ideas.falsifier: Deadline uncertainty is rare, or the intervention only shifts shipping methods without increasing on-time kept purchases.

ideas.title: Publish verified compatibility rules, including explicit non-matches
ideas.buyer: Merchants selling replacement parts, filters, chargers or accessories for specific equipment.
ideas.problem: A fluent product description can imply compatibility from similar model names even when a connector, generation or dimension makes the item unusable.
ideas.mechanism: Discovery and selection: machine-readable supported and excluded model combinations can help a suitable item survive a hard constraint and prevent false-positive purchases. Kept purchases, rather than gross conversion, determine success.
ideas.intervention: Create an approved compatibility graph from manufacturer tables and merchant evidence, with exact model aliases, necessary adapters and explicit incompatible revisions. Export supported facts to existing metafields/feed attributes and render an evidence-backed fit check on the landing page. Treat unknown as unknown.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Codizex Product Fit Finder already offers compatibility selectors; Shopify provides complementary recommendations and Simprosys transports attributes. The opportunity is maintaining authoritative rules across AI discovery and the resulting cart, not inventing fitment filtering.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A narrow vertical with high part-number ambiguity may pay for verified negative constraints and revision handling that generic enrichment cannot safely infer.
dataNeeded: Manufacturer compatibility tables with revision dates
Product/model alias graph and merchant approvals
Pre-purchase model selections and incompatibility return reasons
ideas.experiment: Randomize product families to existing verified facts or the structured compatibility treatment, plus persistently randomized landing checks where separable. Avoid unsupported claims in both arms. Run 8-12 weeks and the return window; sample size must account for family clustering. Primary endpoint: kept compatible AI-origin orders per assigned family-week; guard total purchases and false fit approvals.
ideas.metric: Incremental kept orders per randomized family-week, with wrong-fit refund rate and coverage reported separately. A lower refund rate alone is not evidence of more purchases.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized; fitment tools and related-product infrastructure already exist (fitment, recommendations). No causal estimate for AI-compatible graph publication was found.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative USD 79/month and USD 30 contribution per additional kept order; actual eligible demand unknown.
impactScenario.calculation: Fee-only break-even = 79/30 = 2.63, or 3 extra kept orders; verification labor and any added returns must also be recovered.
impactScenario.range: Includes zero if engines ignore the fields and negative effects if the graph blocks compatible products.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 79/month vertical pilot, with data-entry work priced separately and only after proving the merchant's current fitment workflow misses the case.
ideas.costControl: Use exact lookup and deterministic constraints; reserve model work for alias candidates, never final compatibility assertions.
dependencies: Licensed or merchant-authorized compatibility evidence
A bounded product vertical
Product-family identity and order/return linkage
ideas.failureMode: Evidence is expensive to maintain or misleading aliases produce incorrect exclusions.
ideas.falsifier: Existing fitment tools solve the full journey, or publication plus landing verification yields no additional kept purchases.

ideas.title: Recover sold-out referrals without dropping the shopper's constraints
ideas.buyer: Fashion, homeware and consumables stores with variant stockouts and viable substitutes.
ideas.problem: The referred variant becomes unavailable after indexing; generic recommendations may ignore the size, material, budget or other reason the shopper chose it.
ideas.mechanism: Landing and selection: explicitly acknowledging the stockout and offering a feasible, clearly described substitute can turn an otherwise abandoned AI-origin visit into a kept purchase.
ideas.intervention: On the merchant storefront, preserve known variant constraints, ask one clarifying question only when needed, and rank in-stock alternatives against merchant-approved equivalence rules. Explain each material difference and retain a path to the original product or a consented restock option. Do not silently redirect or substitute a cart item.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Simprosys already syncs availability and excludes variants; Shopify Search & Discovery already recommends related products. The additional hypothesis is hard-constraint preservation for stale external referrals.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A constrained recovery flow beats ordinary related products for a measurable group of stockout arrivals without taking sales away from better-fitting items.
dataNeeded: Requested product/variant and constraints actually available from the referral or shopper
Live stock and merchant-approved substitution relationships
Visitor assignment, all purchased SKUs and return reasons
ideas.experiment: Persistently randomize prequalified AI-referred stockout visitors between the existing out-of-stock page with current recommendations and the constrained recovery flow. Run 6-8 weeks plus returns; power depends on stockout volume. Primary endpoint: any kept purchase per assigned visitor. Guard unsuitable substitutions, complaints, margin and restock subscriptions counted separately.
ideas.metric: All-SKU kept-order probability per randomized stockout visitor; do not count moving an already-likely order to a different SKU as extra conversion.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. Existing native stock-aware recommendations establish overlap (recommendations); OpenAI acknowledges possible update delays (openai-shopping), not a quantified stockout loss rate.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative 500 eligible stockout arrivals/month, USD 29 fee and USD 20 contribution/order.
impactScenario.calculation: Extra kept orders = 500 × observed absolute purchase-probability difference; 1.45 extra orders cover the fee before operating costs.
impactScenario.range: Zero if substitutes fail hard constraints; negative if choice overload or lower-quality substitution increases returns.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 29/month conditional on enough genuine stockout traffic; compare against configuring existing recommendations first.
ideas.costControl: Run deterministic candidate filtering before semantic ranking and only invoke it on real stockout visits.
dependencies: Merchant-owned landing-page integration
Availability of constraints without pretending to read private AI conversations
Substitute inventory and accurate comparison facts
ideas.failureMode: The missing variant was essential, and a recovery panel only delays an inevitable exit.
ideas.falsifier: Existing recommendations perform as well on kept purchases, or treatment only increases low-quality replacement orders and returns.

ideas.title: Quote the payable offer for the actual destination before cart abandonment
ideas.buyer: Cross-border merchants whose product price is attractive but delivery fees, minimum spend or local pricing change the decision.
ideas.problem: The AI-visible item price can fit a budget while the order available to this shopper does not; uncertainty or a late surprise then destroys the purchase.
ideas.mechanism: Selection and checkout: an early, honest estimate can identify a feasible service, quantity or alternative before commitment. It may reduce unsuitable checkouts while increasing completed, kept purchases among shoppers with a feasible offer.
ideas.intervention: Use the shopper's chosen destination and exact variant/quantity to obtain a Shopify cart estimate, including applicable discounts and available delivery choices. State which taxes or duties remain unresolved, timestamp the quote and reconcile it at checkout. Offer optional feasible alternatives; never promise an estimate is final.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Shopify already exposes buyer-aware cart costs; Simprosys already submits Markets feeds, promotions and Google automated discounts. Another price field or coupon engine is insufficient differentiation.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: Joining the published AI offer to the merchant's payable cart catches economically consequential discrepancies that separate feed and checkout tools do not explain.
dataNeeded: Exact variant, quantity and shopper-provided country/postcode
Cart cost components and discount eligibility
Quote-to-checkout discrepancies and kept orders
ideas.experiment: Randomize eligible AI-referred visitors before showing the additional quote; preserve existing mandatory disclosures in both arms. Compare current localized page with the quote workflow for 6-8 weeks plus refund maturation, sized from actual cross-border volume. Primary endpoint: kept purchases per assigned visitor. Guard page latency, margin, estimate error and privacy friction.
ideas.metric: Intent-to-treat kept-order probability among prequalified arrivals; quote acceptance and checkout starts remain diagnostics. Contribution after fulfilment is a guardrail.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized, with documented cart infrastructure and known estimate limitations (cart); existing Markets and discount competition (product, discount).

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative USD 49/month, unknown eligible traffic, and store-measured contribution m.
impactScenario.calculation: Required additional kept orders = (49 + variable quoting cost)/m. Revenue gain without fulfilment and refund costs is not the break-even measure.
impactScenario.range: Can be zero or negative if early cost disclosure merely moves abandonment earlier or the quote step adds friction.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 49/month for stores with measured cost-surprise abandonment; no published willingness-to-pay evidence for this exact intervention.
ideas.costControl: Cache regional rules, use exact cart APIs for selected offers and avoid full-cart simulation for every catalogue item.
dependencies: Authorized Storefront API integration
Correct buyer-country context and reliable shipping configuration
A usable quote when some amounts remain estimates
ideas.failureMode: A partial estimate creates more false certainty than the existing page or demands too much buyer information.
ideas.falsifier: Cost discrepancies are negligible or an adequately powered test shows no rise in kept purchases net of quoting friction.

ideas.title: Make the return commitment understandable for this product and market
ideas.buyer: Merchants whose products have differing customization, hygiene, damage or return-shipping conditions.
ideas.problem: A generic store policy may not answer the shopper's real concern about this item, and an incorrect blanket 'no returns' explanation can obscure rights or discourage a valid purchase.
ideas.mechanism: Selection and checkout: a correct, concise product-specific explanation reduces uncertainty for buyers whose real return rights meet their needs. It must never manufacture a guarantee or weaken statutory rights to raise conversion.
ideas.intervention: Have the merchant approve a policy decision table by jurisdiction and product condition. Generate a short explanation plus source policy link on the landing page and publish appropriate structured labels/FAQs through existing channels. Flag conflicts for review; do not autonomously decide novel legal questions.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Simprosys documents return-policy labels; Shopify already supports policies and Knowledge Base FAQs. The proposed value is item/market-specific consistency and tested comprehension, not policy hosting.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A merchant with complex but legitimate return conditions may gain kept purchases by making existing rights clear at the decision point.
dataNeeded: Current merchant policies and product exceptions
Relevant official jurisdiction guidance reviewed by the merchant
Shopper country, assigned exposures, kept orders and policy disputes
ideas.experiment: Correct any legally misleading baseline universally before testing. Randomize eligible AI-referred visitors between the current accurate full policy and a concise item-specific explanation linking to it. Plan 6-8 weeks plus the applicable return window; power from actual purchase rates. Primary endpoint: kept purchases per assigned visitor. Guard return expense, incorrect explanations and disputes.
ideas.metric: Kept-order probability per randomized visitor, with gross orders, returned orders and complaints separately reported. Comprehension is a mechanism check, not conversion proof.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. UK official guidance supports the distinction between statutory rights and merchant rules (returns); native policy/FAQ tools already exist (ai-policy). No numeric uplift is inferred.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative USD 29/month and measured incremental contribution m after returns; no baseline conversion assumed.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even requires extra kept contribution greater than USD 29 plus policy review cost; more gross orders followed by equivalent returns do not meet it.
impactScenario.range: Zero if customers already understand the policy; negative if clearer restrictions correctly disqualify many shoppers or explanations introduce errors.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 29/month for operationally complex stores; legal review cost is additional and cannot be hidden in a low-price claim.
ideas.costControl: Use approved deterministic policy tables and regenerate only after relevant policy changes.
dependencies: Merchant-approved legal/policy interpretation for a bounded jurisdiction
Accurate product exception tags
Supported destination fields and visible policy sources
ideas.failureMode: The merchant policy is inconsistent, or a generated summary drops a material exception.
ideas.falsifier: Existing native FAQs answer the same questions accurately and the new presentation does not improve kept-order conversion.

ideas.title: Resolve pack and seller identity before AI compares the wrong offer
ideas.buyer: Resellers and manufacturers offering singles, multipacks, kits or refurbished versions of the same named product.
ideas.problem: A cheap single unit can be compared with a multipack, or the wrong maker/condition can be attached to an offer, causing rejection or a mistaken purchase.
ideas.mechanism: Discovery and comparison: correct product identity can place an offer in the right comparison set and make a fair unit-price assessment possible. The purchase effect requires that erroneous identity was actually excluding or misleading prospective buyers.
ideas.intervention: Build a merchant-reviewed identity record linking supplier evidence, GTIN/MPN, pack composition, condition and seller role. Reconcile source feeds, rendered pages and allowed Catalog mappings; distinguish a manufacturer bundle from a merchant-created kit. Verify observed destination grouping and never invent missing identifiers.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Simprosys already covers GTIN/MPN/brand; Google specifies bundle/multipack identity; Shopify already groups identical items and variants. A generic barcode validator is not the product.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: Cross-destination pack and seller-role conflicts persist despite syntactically valid identifiers, and a specialist evidence workflow resolves them cheaply enough to retain more sales.
dataNeeded: Manufacturer/supplier identity and pack evidence
Feed, page and observed destination grouping records
Pack-specific orders, cancellation and wrong-item returns
ideas.experiment: Randomize matched product families with non-urgent identity ambiguity to evidence-backed reconciliation or the current documented review workflow. Immediately correct dangerous or materially false claims in both arms. Use 8-12 weeks after a fixed propagation period; power at family level. Primary endpoint: kept AI-origin orders per family-week; track total orders and incorrect-pack returns.
ideas.metric: Incremental kept orders per assigned family-week; favourable ranking or unit-price display is a diagnostic. Include all items in each family to detect cannibalization.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. Official sources establish complex identity rules and native overlap (upi, simprosys-upi, mapping), not the incidence of broken identity in Simprosys.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative USD 49/month and USD 25 incremental contribution per kept order; prevalence must be audited.
impactScenario.calculation: Fee-only break-even = 49/25 = 1.96, or 2 extra kept orders; supplier verification labor is additional.
impactScenario.range: Zero if downstream systems already resolve the offers correctly; negative if grouping merges genuinely distinct products.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 49/month for high-conflict catalogues; first test whether the merchant will pay for a reproduced identity case.
ideas.costControl: Use deterministic identifier and pack checks, with human review only for conflicting evidence.
dependencies: Reliable supplier evidence and legitimate identifier access
Destination-level observation without claiming control of ranking
Family-level purchase and return measurement
ideas.failureMode: The destination's matching logic ignores corrected fields or the merchant cannot establish authoritative identity.
ideas.falsifier: Most cases are already solved by the feed app or Catalog mapping, or corrected identity fails to produce worthwhile retained-order value.

ideas.title: Check that each AI checkout route can fulfil the actual product requirements
ideas.buyer: Merchants with required custom inputs, checkout apps, bundles or fulfilment options that differ across channels.
ideas.problem: A valid product feed does not guarantee that the selected AI checkout can collect the required information or offer the necessary fulfilment method.
ideas.mechanism: Checkout completion: identifying route incompatibility before exposure and moving supported validation to server logic can prevent dead-end or invalid orders. A supported merchant checkout can preserve sales when an embedded route cannot meet requirements.
ideas.intervention: Inventory required product and checkout capabilities, compare them with each channel's current contract, and replay approved sandbox carts through the supported path. Port permissible validations to Shopify Functions where appropriate; keep unsupported product flows on a permitted storefront route. Do not claim an app can force an AI engine to render unsupported components.
ideas.competitorOverlap: Simprosys already has direct-checkout setup. Shopify explicitly documents unsupported Google direct-checkout product types, delivery methods and some blocks, with Functions support. The gap is merchant-specific verification of app dependencies and a tested fallback.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: A small specialist can recover revenue from a narrow set of compatibility failures that feed validation and generic channel eligibility do not fully diagnose.
dataNeeded: Product requirements and checkout-app inventory
Versioned channel capability constraints and sandbox traces
Channel-attributed completed orders, invalid orders and refunds
ideas.experiment: Randomize matched eligible stores to compatibility remediation or current onboarding/support, because checkout-channel settings are often store-level. Repair severe errors immediately in both arms. Run 8-12 weeks or longer until the predeclared store-cluster sample is reached. Primary endpoint: kept AI-origin orders per randomized store-week, adjusted for pre-period levels. Guard all-channel orders, loss of useful direct checkout, unsupported item sales and checkout latency.
ideas.metric: Difference in kept AI-origin orders per assigned store-week; keep unsupported-product exposure and invalid orders as diagnostics. Use Shopify order records rather than relying only on storefront pixels.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized. Shopify documents real capability and pixel limitations (google-ai); no evidence establishes their prevalence or incremental revenue under this proposed repair process.

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative USD 99/month, unknown affected volume, contribution m after fulfilment/refunds.
impactScenario.calculation: Break-even extra kept orders = (99 + remediation cost amortized monthly)/m; at illustrative m = USD 30 the subscription alone needs 3.3, or 4 whole orders.
impactScenario.range: Negative if fallback loses the benefits of a working direct checkout; zero if native support already handles every important requirement.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 99/month or a separately scoped one-off repair fee, tested only after demonstrating an unresolved checkout dependency.
ideas.costControl: Maintain reusable channel capability tests and rerun affected tests after app/configuration changes; do not replay every product.
dependencies: Merchant-authorized checkout configuration and app access
Supported sandbox/testing paths and order-ledger access
Enough merchants for store-level randomization
ideas.failureMode: There is no supported fallback with comparable convenience, or the merchant cannot alter a critical third-party app.
ideas.falsifier: Audit finds no material route incompatibility beyond native checks, or remediation reduces total kept AI-origin purchases.

ideas.title: Spend the next repair hour on changes that survive an order holdout
ideas.buyer: Agencies and merchants with many feed suggestions but limited implementation time.
ideas.problem: Cheap feed optimization creates more possible edits than a team can investigate, while simulated recommendation rates can rank work incorrectly.
ideas.mechanism: Enabling mechanism: better allocation can cause more purchases only by choosing and deploying changes with higher real incremental kept-order effects under the same implementation budget. A dashboard alone has no purchase effect.
ideas.intervention: Use a frozen, merchant-owned retrieval replay to diagnose which facts change model decisions, preserve repeated runs as model-variance checks, and nominate bounded repairs. Validate candidates in merchant-controlled live randomized rollouts, join assignment to the order ledger, and update a repair priority policy only from held-out purchase evidence. Keep paid-shopping and AI-shopping results separate.
ideas.competitorOverlap: DataFeedWatch already offers product-title A/B allocation; Simprosys advises A/B testing and provides purchase tracking and campaign metrics. Shopify provides channel/referrer order attribution. The possible advantage is a validated allocation policy for retained AI-origin orders, not the A/B button.
ideas.edgeHypothesis: Across repeated merchants and issue types, a low-cost diagnostic plus holdout workflow selects materially better work than prioritizing error counts or simulated recommendation deltas.
dataNeeded: Representative shopper intents and fixed retrieval snapshots
Exact source edits, propagation observations and randomization assignments
Order/refund ledger, source-quality flags, implementation hours and tool costs
ideas.experiment: First A/A-check assignment and order joins. Then randomize merchants to purchase-evidence prioritization or their current issue-ranking workflow with equal repair hours and paid budget. Run at least 12 weeks and meet a store-cluster power target; sparse AI demand may require a larger pooled cohort. Primary endpoint: kept AI-origin orders per store-week. Guard all-channel purchases, contribution, analyst time and consent-related missingness.
ideas.metric: Intent-to-treat order difference per randomized store-week; cost per incremental kept order is reported only when the incremental-order estimate is positive and sufficiently precise. Do not sum improvements from overlapping repairs.
ideas.impactEvidence: Hypothesized indirect effect. Existing A/B and tracking features are documented (dfw-ab, ga4, zombie). Proprietary consumer behavior is not reproduced by arbitrary custom tools (openai-shopping).

impactScenario.baseline: Illustrative USD 79/month, equal implementation hours in both arms, unknown incremental purchases.
impactScenario.calculation: Net incremental contribution = held-out extra kept orders × measured contribution/order - USD 79 - incremental measurement/repair costs. A simulated recommendation delta contributes zero to this calculation.
impactScenario.range: Can be zero when there is too little AI-origin traffic to learn, or negative when proxy-driven prioritization sends effort to the wrong fixes.

ideas.willingnessToPay: Unvalidated USD 79/month per merchant, or agency pilot priced against demonstrably better allocation; no claim that small stores can power it.
ideas.costControl: Deterministic screening, cached retrievals, stratified intent samples and sequential compute budgets; increase model calls only when the decision could change.
dependencies: A genuine implementation channel for nominated repairs
Reliable order assignments and a large enough merchant cohort
Predeclared analysis, contamination checks and treatment propagation rules
ideas.failureMode: The harness learns its own synthetic shopper preferences, missing provenance biases outcomes, or shared inventory and campaigns contaminate arms.
ideas.falsifier: Offline scores do not predict held-out purchase effects and the allocation policy fails to beat the existing workflow at equal effort.

sources.title: Simprosys Google Shopping Feed - Shopify App Store
sources.claim: 29 September 2026 snapshot: 4.9 rating from 4,894 reviews, launch date 16 August 2017, published plan prices and qualitative support experiences. Reviews are not controlled conversion evidence.

sources.title: Pricing for Simprosys Google Shopping Feed
sources.claim: Published-product billing excludes variant counts, includes a 21-day first-install trial, and documents monthly tiers and add-ons. Prices observed 29 September 2026, USD.

sources.title: Shopify Google Shopping Feed App by Simprosys
sources.claim: Vendor claims 90K+ Shopify merchants and documents feed rules, channel integrations, campaigns, Markets, discounts and support. Reach is self-reported; no audited profit or causal uplift.

sources.title: Enable AI-powered Feed Optimisation in Simprosys Google Shopping Feed for Shopify
sources.claim: English and category eligibility, description length over 200 characters, minimum USD 1/25 products, manual review or automatic submission, and no automatic re-optimisation after product updates.

sources.title: Setup Google Calculated Delivery Speed Estimates from Simprosys Google Shopping Feed App for Shopify
sources.claim: Order-tracking data integration for Google delivery estimates; the guide describes US merchant availability and order exclusions. This is an existing feature, not measured incremental sales.

sources.title: How to Enable the Direct Checkout Feature for Google Free Listings
sources.claim: Simprosys publishes a direct-checkout setup tutorial. The page is video-led; it does not establish full parity with newer AI-channel checkout requirements.

sources.title: How to Enable Server-side Google Analytics 4 tracking using GTM
sources.claim: Existing GA4/GTM tracking and selectable purchase-value definitions. Tracking setup does not itself identify incremental treatment effects or eliminate missing attribution.

sources.title: Setup Google Ads Zombie SKUs Campaign through Simprosys Google Shopping Feed App
sources.claim: Existing PMAX workflow selects products using impressions, clicks and conversions and reports campaign performance. Paid-ad optimization is not evidence about AI recommendations.

sources.title: Google Automated Discounts: Eligibility & Requirements Explained
sources.claim: Documents an existing Google discount integration; do not pitch automated discount submission as a missing Simprosys feature.

sources.title: Product Feed Optimisation: An Ultimate Checklist to Drive Traffic, Clicks & Conversions
sources.claim: Vendor advice includes A/B testing. Advice alone does not document an in-app randomized experiment or AI simulation harness.

sources.title: Verified Merchant Reviews from Major Platforms | Simprosys
sources.claim: Vendor-curated merchant reports describe support, faster syncing, time savings and sales improvement without controlled denominators or counterfactuals.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | Selling on Google AI Mode and Gemini
sources.claim: Merchant Center, including third-party feeds, powers discovery. Documents direct-checkout eligibility, unsupported product/delivery types, pixel limitations and checkout customization constraints.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | Selling on ChatGPT
sources.claim: Shopify Catalog powers the Shopify ChatGPT channel; purchase occurs through the merchant's online checkout. This specific integration differs from general OpenAI checkout possibilities.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | Mapping your product data sources for Shopify Catalog
sources.claim: Native preferred-source mappings, metafields, variant grouping and preview already exist; processing is delayed and mappings influence rather than guarantee output.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | Optimizing your products for AI platforms
sources.claim: Native guidance covers structured product information, current policies and Knowledge Base FAQs. Basic policy publication is already supported.

sources.title: A/B Testing Product Titles for Better Ads Performance
sources.claim: DataFeedWatch already assigns A/B title structures across item IDs and adds URL tracking. Documentation gives alternating item-ID allocation; it does not prove shopper randomization for the same product.

sources.title: Add a checkout link for your products - Google Merchant Center Help
sources.claim: Variant-specific checkout URLs and recurring Google validation already exist. Necessary warnings can be bypassed when a shopper skips the product page.

sources.title: How to fix: Inaccurate price status due to inconsistency between feed and landing page
sources.claim: Google requires consistency and recommends variant-specific preselection; feed/landing discrepancies are a known problem, not evidence of their prevalence in Simprosys stores.

sources.title: Handling cutoff time [handling_cutoff_time] - Google Merchant Center Help
sources.claim: Product/country cutoff and timezone controls already exist. A deadline intervention must add live operational verification, not merely another cutoff field.

sources.title: About unique product identifiers - Google Merchant Center Help
sources.claim: Documents distinct identifier treatment for manufacturer-created and merchant-created bundles/multipacks. Correct identity must be established from evidence.

sources.title: Unique Product Identifiers: GTIN, MPN and Brand
sources.claim: Simprosys already provides identifier guidance; generic GTIN cleanup is not an empty market.

sources.title: Accepting returns and giving refunds: the law - GOV.UK
sources.claim: UK guidance distinguishes statutory rights, sale items and distance-selling returns, with exceptions. Supports a narrowly scoped policy check, not universal legal assurance.

sources.title: Create and update a cart with the Storefront API
sources.claim: Carts support exact merchandise, buyer country, delivery preferences and estimated costs; checkout remains authoritative and estimates may change.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | Customize product recommendations with Shopify Search & Discovery
sources.claim: Native related/complementary product recommendations already exist, with stock rules and merchant-selected metafields.

sources.title: Codizex - Product Fit Finder - Shopify App Store
sources.claim: An adjacent vendor already sells configurable compatibility selectors and product-page fit checks. Its absolute no-wrong-purchase marketing claim is not accepted as empirical evidence.

sources.title: Shopping with ChatGPT Search
sources.claim: Selection depends on intent/context and multiple metadata/content sources; prices and shipping can lag. Public documentation does not disclose the full production ranking system.

sources.title: Shopify Help Center | Shopify agentic storefronts
sources.claim: Documents channel/referrer attribution on orders and differences among discovery/referral and direct-checkout channels. Attribution does not establish incrementality.

sources.title: Optional Attributes and Specifications in Google Shopping Feed
sources.claim: Simprosys documents return-policy labels, physical dimensions, certification, promotions and free-shipping threshold attributes. These are existing feed capabilities.
